keyword_results.evidence: Two curved stitched panel lines are visible on the teal bodice from the upper bodice beside the neckline, over the bust, to the fitted waist seam. Their relief/stitched continuity belongs to the dress, rather than a print.
The teal bodice upper boundary forms two rounded lobes meeting at a clear center depression above the central front seam. It is a garment edge, separate from the necklace.
Both sleeves have pronounced gathered shoulder and upper-arm volume, tapering into close-fitting elbow-to-wrist lower sleeves and cuffs attached to the same dress.
Both hip pocket mouths are narrow horizontal dark slits framed by slim matching fabric lips. They are inset into the skirt/dress, remain clear of hands, and do not read as patch or flap pockets.

Ivory edging follows the neckline and both cuff boundaries, but at native scale the visible trim reads as a narrow light band. Its raised cord-like cross-section is not distinguishable confidently from flat binding. The required dimensional relation is unconfirmed.
keyword_results.native_region: neckline in bodice crop and cuff crop

keyword_results.evidence: Two outer front-skirt fold edges turn toward the center and meet at the upper stitched front section; below them a darker recessed underfold is exposed between the edges. The center is recessed rather than a projecting box panel or open bare slit.

A small silver connector is present above the rectangular pendant and the necklace descends toward it. The connector spans only a few native pixels; a separate open bail and the chain passing through its opening cannot be resolved. A top connection alone does not prove the specified bail topology.

Both black shoe uppers remain in frame. On the forward shoe, separate eyelet-bearing quarters visibly sit above the vamp with open V edges surrounding the tongue and laces; the rear shoe also shows open lacing.

additional_test_gates.evidence: All declared garment/jewelry regions are present in one frame, but the bail topology and cord relief are unconfirmed at native resolution.
Body ownership, articulation and floor support pass; critical jewelry contact and its visibility remain unconfirmed.

The output uses a short dark bob with fine fringe and similar visible face presentation. Clothing and scene come from the authored concept. This is appearance comparison only, not identity, ethnicity, personality, body-shape or actual-age inference.

embodiment_body_ownership.evidence: The visible head, both arms, hands, legs and shoes connect to one coherent foreground adult wearer. The dress, necklace and shoes are worn by that same subject.

embodiment_joint_chain_and_reach.evidence: Both upper arms connect to the shoulders, forearms taper to the cuffs, and each hand continues from its wrist. The relaxed arm reach beside the hips is coherent and no major segment is detached.

embodiment_support_and_balance.evidence: The modest staggered/crossed standing stance has both shoe soles contacting the level floor, with plausible contact shadows and the torso balanced above the supporting feet.

embodiment_contact_and_space.evidence: Hands clear the pocket mouths and shoe-floor contacts are coherent, but the required necklace-chain-through-bail contact remains too small to assess. This is an unconfirmed intended contact, not a diagnosis of malformed anatomy.

embodiment_visibility_and_projection.evidence: The full frame includes head, garment front, sleeves, hands, skirt folds and both shoe uppers. The tiny pendant connector does not provide enough native pixels to assess the critical chain-through-loop relation.

control_comparison: The composed gaze and fitted tailoring plausibly carry subtle supporting sensual appeal within the whole portrayal. This is a qualitative impression, not a measured intensity or user acceptance; no distinctive fetish or surreal treatment was added.
causality_boundary: The run establishes actual exposure/adoption and pixel fidelity of this one saved result; it does not prove a causal improvement over a candidate-free image or general retrieval coverage.
